title: Max Consecutive Ones III
prompt: Given a binary array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the maximum number of consecutive `1`'s in the array if you can flip at most `k` `0`'s to `1`'s.

examples.explanation: Flip the two 0's at indices 5 and 4 (or similar) to get [1,1,1,0,0,1,1,1,1,1,1], the longest run of 1's has length 6.
All elements are 0 and no flips are allowed, so the longest run of 1's is 0

hints: This is equivalent to finding the longest window that contains at most k zeros.
Use a variable-size sliding window with a running count of zeros inside it.
Expand right always; when the zero count exceeds k, shrink from the left until it's at most k again, tracking the max window length throughout (never shrink the max, only the window itself).

solution.approach: Flipping at most k zeros to ones means we want the longest window that contains at most k zeros — those zeros are exactly what we'd flip. Use a sliding window with a zero counter: always expand right by one, and whenever the zero count exceeds k, advance the left pointer (decrementing the zero counter when a zero leaves) until the window is valid again. The window never needs to shrink below the best length found, so track the max window size throughout the single pass.
